recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片上可見一條長而彎曲的線狀寄生蟲，蟲體內充滿一列列紫色核柱，一端延伸出淡粉紅色、不含核的鞘狀構造，大小遠超過周圍紅血球，符合微絲蟲（microfilaria）；結合臨床為班氏絲蟲（Wuchereria bancrofti）。
features: Elongated, curved worm-like organism many times the length of a red cell
Body filled with densely packed purple-staining nuclei arranged in a column
Pale pink sheath-like extension beyond the nuclear column at one end
Gentle curves with a coiled segment at one end
Adjacent smudged pink-purple cellular debris and pale red cell ghosts in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single elongated, gracefully curved microfilaria many times the length of a red cell, with a column of densely packed purple somatic nuclei. A pale pink, anucleate sheath-like extension projects beyond the nuclear column at one end, and adjacent smudged cellular debris is present. Species-level features such as the tail-tip nuclei are difficult to assess in this photograph. In the clinical context, findings are consistent with microfilaremia due to Wuchereria bancrofti.

ddx.vs: Brugia microfilariae are sheathed but have kinked curves, a sheath that stains pink with Giemsa, and two separate terminal nuclei at the tail tip.
Loa loa is sheathed with nuclei extending continuously to the tail tip and is found in daytime blood in Central/West Africa.
Mansonella microfilariae are small, unsheathed, and have nuclei extending to a blunt tail tip.
Fibers lack internal nuclei and a defined cephalic space and are refractile rather than stained.
